claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy has coarse dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Internal boundaries in the coarse lamellar colonies enable microcrack initiation during tensile deformation.
Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can engineer an ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The tailored thermo-mechanical route consists specifically of rolling followed by controlled annealing.
The ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure can inherit or preserve the alloy's composite lamellar nature.
Ultrafine grain boundaries impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
Retained lamellar interfaces impede crack propagation and act as microcrack-arresting features.
The processed heterogeneous duplex structure produces a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The processed microstructure generates a microcrack-arresting mechanism that delays damage accumulation.
Relative to the coarse lamellar baseline, processing will increase tensile strength at room temperature.
Relative to the coarse lamellar baseline, processing will increase tensile ductility at room temperature.
The processed alloy will be less susceptible to catastrophic room-temperature tensile failure.
The simultaneous benefits occur only within an optimized range of thermo-mechanical processing parameters.
Excessive deformation or inappropriate annealing may cause phase transformations or coarsening that negate the improvements.
The exact processing parameters and quantitative property improvements remain insufficiently established.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in both tensile strength and strain to failure relative to a conventionally processed control would falsify the hypothesis.
